extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent attorneys/agents, USPTO examiners, and third-party reexamination requesters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for handling ex parte reexamination proceedings before the USPTO, covering duties of disclosure, interviews, notification of prior/concurrent proceedings, consolidation/merger of multiple reexaminations, interactions with interferences/reissue proceedings, fees, and related petition practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure under 37 CFR 1.555
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals (third-party requesters, their attorneys/agents, and patent owners/owners' attorneys or agents) have the responsibility of compliance with 37 CFR 1.555 and must disclose information material to patentability in the reexamination proceeding to the attorney/agent responsible for the reexamination or to the patent owner acting on his/her own behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney, agent, or patent owner who receives information has no duty to submit such information if it is not material to patentability in the reexamination proceeding. See 37 CFR 1.555(b) for the definition of 'material to patentability.' Fraud or bad faith/intentional misconduct in failing to comply results in noncompliance with 37 CFR 1.555(a). Failure to comply risks diminishing the quality and reliability of the reexamination certificate. This duty is consistent with duty under 37 CFR 1.56. See MPEP § 2282 and § 2686 for related duties to disclose prior or concurrent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews must be conducted in the Office during Office hours (37 CFR 1.560(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews in ex parte reexamination proceedings between examiners and patent owners or their attorneys/agents of record must be conducted in the Office at times within Office hours as designated by the examiner; interviews will not be permitted at other times/places without Director authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should be arranged in advance. Interviews for discussion of the patentability of claims will not be conducted prior to the first official action except in limited circumstances where the examiner initiates an interview to provide an amendment to make claims patentable and the patent owner's role is passive (limited to agreeing to the change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests by third-party requesters to participate in interviews will not be granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests that reexamination requesters participate in interviews with examiners will not be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ex parte reexamination only the patent owner (and/or the patent owner's representative) may have interviews with the examiner. Third-party requesters may not attend or participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner must file a written statement of interview (37 CFR 1.560(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In every instance of an interview with an examiner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written statement must be filed either as a separate part of a response to an outstanding Office action or as a separate paper within one month from the date of the interview, whichever is later. The requirement cannot be waived by the examiner. Failure to file the written statement as required will result in termination of the reexamination prosecution (analogous to failure to timely respond to an Office action). A patent owner's response to an outstanding Office action after an interview does not remove the necessity for filing the written statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners shall limit discussions with non-owners to strictly procedural matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any party who is not the patent owner requests information as to the merits of a reexamination proceeding, the examiner will not conduct a personal or telephone interview to provide such information; only questions on strictly procedural matters may be discussed with that party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines to determine procedural matters: (A) any information which a person could obtain by reading the file (open to the public) is procedural and may be discussed; (B) matters not available from a reading of the file are considered relating to the merits and may not be discussed. Example: when the next Office action will be rendered is a merits-related question and should not be responded to by the examiner for a non-owner party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must complete Interview Summary form PTOL-474 when substantive matter discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must complete an Interview Summary form PTOL-474 for each interview held where a matter of substance has been discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the form should be given to the patent owner at the conclusion of the interview; the original should be made of record in the reexamination file, and a copy should be mailed to any third party requester. See MPEP §§ 713.01–713.04 for general procedure and recording interview summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of prior or concurrent proceedings (37 CFR 1.565(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: In an ex parte reexamination proceeding the patent owner must inform the Office of any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved (e.g., interferences, reissues, ex parte reexaminations, inter partes reexaminations, litigation) and the results of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will accept copies of notices of suits and other proceedings and copies of decisions or papers filed in court for entry into the reexamination file to ensure a complete file with updated status information. Persons must limit such submissions to notification only and not include further arguments or information; submissions not so limited will be returned. Proper submissions will be entered into the record and considered by the examiner when the proceeding comes up for action on the merits. IDSs submitted in litigation discovery and properly filed under 37 CFR 1.565(a) may be entered and considered. Use form paragraphs (¶ 22.07, ¶ 22.08) as litigation reminders when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions of notices must be limited to bare notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission is not limited to bare notice of the prior or concurrent proceedings, the submission will be returned by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only notification documents (not further arguments) should be filed for entry into the reexamination file. Proper submissions will be entered and considered when the proceeding comes up for action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second/subsequent ex parte reexamination request must raise a substantial new question of patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for a second or subsequent request for ex parte reexamination to be granted while a prior ex parte reexamination is pending, a substantial new question of patentability must be raised by the art (patents and/or printed publications) cited in the later request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP § 2240 discusses when a substantial new question is raised. The second request should be decided promptly; it should be processed quickly and assigned to the same examiner as the first request where practicable. Request 2 should be decided immediately without waiting the usual period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merging/combining copending ex parte reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.565(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If ex parte reexamination is ordered while a prior ex parte reexamination is pending and prosecution in the prior proceeding has not been terminated, the ex parte reexamination proceedings will be consolidated and result in issuance of a single certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision whether to combine is made by the Technology Center (TC) Director (may delegate to TC SPRE). No decision to combine should be made until reexamination is actually ordered in the later-filed request. If merged, prosecution continues at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding; a single combined examiner's action will be prepared listing both control numbers. When merged, files are maintained as separate complete files but require identical claims or the patent owner given 1 month to amend to make claims identical. If claims are not identical after that period, non-identical claims should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as indefinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of Request 2 and storage pending statements/replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Request 2 should be processed as quickly as possible and assigned to the same examiner as Request 1; Request 2 should be decided immediately and, if granted, its order mailed immediately. The two requests should be held in storage until the patent owner's statement and any reply by the requester have been received in Request 2 or until the time for filing expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Request 2 is denied, prosecution on Request 1 should continue. If Request 2 is granted, the TC Director or delegate will prepare a decision merging the two proceedings. Request 2 should be determined on its own merits and should not rely on the decision in Request 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for merged proceeding filings and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When proceedings are merged the decision should require that the patent owner maintain identical claims in both files, and responses and other papers must consist of a single response filed in duplicate, each signed and containing identifying data for both files for entry in both files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the merger decision requires an amendment to make claims identical and the patent owner fails to timely submit it, any claim not identical in all merged proceedings should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as indefinite. Clerical and printing procedures (e.g., action cover form, PALM printer, PTOL-465 transmission form) must follow merged-file process. If multiple requests (>2) are filed, extend guidelines accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed which requires payment of a fee (e.g., excess claim fee, extension of time request, petition fee, appeal fee, brief fee, oral hearing fee), only a single fee need be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: only one fee is required for an appeal brief even though copies must be filed for each file in the merged proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: No petition necessary to merge multiple copending reexaminations; premature petitions returned
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge is necessary since the Office will generally sua sponte make a decision as to whether to merge multiple reexamination proceedings. If a petition to merge is filed prior to the determination (37 CFR 1.515) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) on the second request, it will not be considered and will be returned to the submitting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision returning a premature petition will be made of record in both reexamination files but no copy of the petition will be retained by the Office. After order to reexamine, the patent owner may file a petition to merge as part of the patent owner's statement (37 CFR 1.530). Petitions by parties other than the patent owner or one of the requesters will not be considered and will be returned as improper under 37 CFR 1.550(g). All merger decisions on the merits will be made by the TC Director (or delegate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination ordinarily will not be delayed because of an interference (special dispatch under 35 U.S.C. 305)
rubrics_metrics.description: General Office policy is that a reexamination proceeding will not be delayed or stayed because of an interference or the possibility of an interference, due to the requirement that reexamination proceedings be conducted with 'special dispatch.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will generally make required decisions in the reexamination and proceed with the interference to the extent desirable. Decisions in the interference will take into consideration the status of the reexamination and may be tailored by the Board (37 CFR 41.103). Note: a reexamination proceeding itself can never be 'involved' in an interference because it is neither an application nor a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when applicant attempts to provoke an interference with a patent under reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is filed in a pending application seeking to provoke an interference with a patent involved in reexamination, the applicant must comply with 37 CFR 41.202(a), including identifying the patent under reexamination with which interference is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding application claims may be rejected on any applicable grounds, including prior art cited in the reexamination proceeding. Prosecution of the application should continue as far as possible. If the application is placed in condition for allowance but still contains claims which interfere with claims of the patent under reexamination, an interference should ordinarily be proposed; the examiner must notify the Office of Patent Legal Administration (OPLA) before proposing the interference and may not propose it unless authorized by OPLA. If interference is not authorized, further action on the application should be suspended until the reexamination certificate issues and is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion/request to suspend interference pending reexamination (37 CFR 41.121(a)(3) and 1.565(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A miscellaneous motion under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(3) to suspend an interference pending the outcome of a reexamination may be made at any time during the interference by any party, and will be decided by the administrative patent judge based on the particular facts; suspension is not favored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally no consideration will be given unless a reexamination order is issued; if the motion is denied by the administrative patent judge, a request to stay the interference may be made to the Director under 37 CFR 1.565(e). A request to stay under 1.565(e) will be decided by the Chief Administrative Patent Judge of the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing for reexamination during interference and required notices to the Board (37 CFR 1.510(a) and 41.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file a request for reexamination during the enforceability of a patent. Under 37 CFR 41.8(a), the patent owner must identify its real party-in-interest and each judicial or administrative proceeding that could affect or be affected by the Board proceeding, and must notify the Board within 20 days of any change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the patent owner files the reexamination request, the 20-day period runs from the filing date. The patent owner must notify the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences that a request for reexamination was filed within 20 days of receiving notice of the request. Such reexamination requests will be processed normally. If an examiner orders reexamination and subsequently rejects a patent claim corresponding to a count in the interference, the Board shall be called to that fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action in interference following reexamination certificate issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more claims of a patent involved in an interference are canceled or amended by issuance and publication of a reexamination certificate, the Board must be promptly notified and the patent owner must notify the administrative patent judge upon issuance and publication of the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the certificate issues, the examiner and Board should review the certificate to determine if changes affect interference status; if so, propose or adjust interference accordingly per MPEP Chapter 2300.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to stay reexamination because of interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to stay a reexamination proceeding because of an interference that is filed prior to the determination (37 CFR 1.515) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) will not be considered and will be returned to the submitting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such returned petitions will be made of record in the reexamination file but no copy will be retained. A petition to stay may be filed by the patent owner as part of the patent owner's statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or thereafter. Petitions filed subsequent to the date of the order for reexamination will be referred to OPLA for decision; all decisions on merits of petitions to stay due to interference will be made in OPLA.
